entityDescription: About the Institute Our cosmic home is the main focus of the scientific research performed in the Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research (MPS): the solar system with its planets and moons, its comets and asteroids, and of course with the Sun. The researchers develop and build scientific instruments for investigating these bodies in cooperation with engineers who are highly qualified and experienced specialists. The instruments are mainly used in outer space, which is made possible through the institute’s collaboration in numerous missions of international space agencies such as ESA and NASA. The data analysis and interpretation is complemented by theoretical models and simulations. The Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research succeeded the Max Planck Institute for Aeronomy in 2004 by a simple name change. The institute was founded in 1957 in Katlenburg-Lindau. Recently, the institute's location was moved to Göttingen. The institute's new home can be found close to the Northern Campus of the University of Göttingen. The institute is organized in three scientific departments.

entityDescription:
In a nutshell, PREDICT Services is an innovative company created in 2006 by Airbus Defense & Space, BRL and Météo France, combining hydrometeorology, telecommunications, space imagery and expertise in risk management to provide real-time decision-making support to cope with natural hazards (before, during and after the events).

We provide a preventive service for local communities (30 000 over 36 000 in France), international companies, industries, insurance companies, national civil protection services and individual users. Our assistance adapts to the situation being based on vulnerability assessment, risk monitoring and graduated warning dissemination. 

PREDICT Services’ experts watch continuously over users in order to inform them when any natural hazard threatens their territory: a 24/7 monitoring service for French homeland and overseas territories, more than 350 industrial sites in 35 countries, and an international expertise already applied in Argentina, Brazil, Djibouti, Haiti, Morocco, Nigeria, Senegal and Rwanda. Predict has been named Expert Partner by the World Bank, the Inter-American Development Bank and the European Commission.

entityDescription:
Integrated Fiber Optics specializes on R&D and small batch production of fiber optics components for fiber lasers and special components of fibers. Main activities are: Components of fibers (for fiber lasers, telecommunications, measure instruments and special components of fibers); Integration and combination of fiber lasers; Optical frequency converters for fiber lasers; Designing of fiber amplifiers (LMA, PCF, CCC fiber based) and their integration into the laser systems of high power and pulse energy; Ultra precise CNC micro machining, micro bounding-assembling and laser micro-spot welding. 
Integrated Fiber Optics in collaboration with Center for Physical Sciences & Technology developed and offers patented ultra-short optical pulse fiber generator-oscillator based on novel patented optical pulse fiber generator technology. Main advantages provided by this technology are high stability of laser parameters, high reliability and long life-time without need for maintenance. These properties are particularly attractive for industrial applications, which is ideal for fiber MOPA (master oscillator power amplifier) seeding and industrial application where reliability, durability and long life-time are essential. Generator does not contain any critical components such as SESAM and so its life-time mainly depends on life-time of a pump diode laser. Generator can operate under normal, zero and anomalous dispersion conditions. Moreover, our developed technology is very flexible and allows achieving of different pulse parameters which could be required for specific customer applications. Ultra-short optical pulse fiber generator-oscillator is protected under Japan patent JP6276471 (B2), United States patent US10038297B2 and Republic of Lithuania patent LT6261 (B), also published as applications CN106575849 (A), EP3178137 (A1), WO2016020188 (A1).
The company also develops highly stable fiber optic components whose characteristics are practically unaffected by temperature changes (insertion losses due to temperature changes of 30 dB).
